ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a histogram titled "Histogram of X", with the horizontal axis labeled X and the vertical axis labeled Frequency. On the horizontal axis, adjacent bars/tick centers can be seen labeled as 7.5, 10.0, 12.5, etc., among which the question asks about the bar whose center is labeled 10. Reasoning: The centers of the bars adjacent to the bar centered at 10 are 7.5 and 12.5 respectively, so the interval between the centers of adjacent bars is 2.5. In the histogram, the range of each bar extends from the center to both sides by half an interval, namely 2.5 ÷ 2 = 1.25. Therefore, the data range represented by the bar centered at 10 is from 10 - 1.25 to 10 + 1.25, that is, from 8.75 to 11.25.

raw_record.question_text: Data values represented by the bar labeled "10" in the histogram below fall into which range?

method.method_draft: Inspect the histogram’s x-axis and identify the bar whose center is labeled 10. Read the neighboring bar centers/tick labels around it: the adjacent bars are centered at 7.5 and 12.5, so the spacing between bar centers is 2.5. Since histogram bars represent intervals extending halfway to the neighboring bin centers, take half of 2.5, which is 1.25. Subtract and add 1.25 from the center label 10 to get the bin range: 8.75 up to 11.25.
